findings.title: The 8 "pre-existing" reminder failures are an expired date fixture, not an implementation bug
findings.evidence: The implementation gates on a strictly-future appointment: `app/(dashboard)/chat/actions.ts:247` is `gt(appointments.startsAt, new Date())`, and line 271 is `if (!appointment) return { ok: false, error: 'Nuk ka takim të ardhshëm.' };`. The test's `beforeEach` seeds a hardcoded fixture at `app/(dashboard)/chat/__tests__/actions.integration.test.ts:336-337`: `startsAt: new Date('2026-08-01T09:00:00.000Z'), endsAt: new Date('2026-08-01T10:00:00.000Z')` (and line 670 seeds the second conversation's appointment at `2026-08-02T09:00:00.000Z`). There are no fake timers anywhere in the file — no `vi.useFakeTimers`/`vi.setSystemTime` — and `tests/setup/global.ts` only migrates and truncates `auth.users`. Today is 2026-08-13, so that fixture is in the past and the appointment subquery returns zero rows for every test. The describe block at line 308 contains exactly 9 tests. Eight of them assert behaviour that happens after the appointment lookup and therefore now receive `{ ok: false, error: 'Nuk ka takim të ardhshëm.' }`. The single exception is `it('refuses the manual send to a patient who opted out of reminders')` (line 503), whose expected error comes from the opt-out guard at `actions.ts:216-218` — which runs BEFORE the `Promise.all` appointment lookup — so it still passes. 9 tests minus 1 = the exactly 8 failures recorded in the log. The regression window is provable from the log itself: the 2026-08-01 entry (progress.md:158) records "587 unit + 606 integration green, full re-run", and the 2026-08-04 entry (progress.md:82) is the first to record "the 8 pre-existing sendUpcomingReminderTemplate failures" — i.e. the suite broke at the instant the fixture timestamp 2026-08-01T09:00:00Z passed.
findings.impact: This is a broken TEST, not a broken implementation — I could not find any defect in `sendUpcomingReminderTemplateImpl`, and I want to be explicit about that so the finding is not misread. The harm is what the dead tests stopped guarding. Eight assertions over the most money- and patient-sensitive path in the product have been vacuous for 12 days and were normalised as "unrelated" in three separate decision-log entries. Specifically unprotected right now: the monthly reminder cap is enforced before a billed Meta template is sent (`refuses the send once the monthly reminder quota is exhausted`); the PT-scoped advisory lock actually prevents two conversations from both consuming the last quota slot (`serializes quota consumption across two conversations`, explicitly labelled a W4 regression test); a persistence failure returns "sent but not saved" rather than the "try again" copy that would lure the PT into paying for a second template; the manual send writes a `reminder_jobs` row so the patient's KONFIRMO/ANULO correlates and the plan meter counts it; the manual stamp leaves `inngestRunId`/`scheduledFor` intact so the sleeping Inngest run does not trip `stale_run` and rewrite the row to `skipped`. Every one of those failure modes is either a wrong bill or a patient reply that silently matches nothing. Any regression introduced into this path between 2026-08-01 and launch would be invisible.
findings.fix_sketch: Make the fixture relative to wall-clock instead of absolute, which is also what the implementation semantically requires. In the `beforeEach` at line 334, use `startsAt: new Date(Date.now() + 7 * 86_400_000)` with a matching `endsAt`, hoist that value into a variable, and reuse it at line 435 where `formatAppointmentTime(new Date('2026-08-01T09:00:00.000Z'), pt.timezone)` computes the expected template variable. Do the same for the second appointment at line 670. Prefer this over `vi.setSystemTime`, because `seedDeliveredReminders` stamps `deliveredAt: new Date()` and `getReminderUsage` buckets by the current calendar month — pinning the clock would require both to move together. Then run `pnpm test:integration` and confirm 9/9 in this file and 64/64 files, so the log entry can be closed rather than carried again.

findings.title: No automated test run exists: pre-commit runs only lint + typecheck, and there is no CI
findings.evidence: `.husky/pre-commit` contains exactly two lines — `pnpm lint` and `pnpm typecheck` — and there is no `.husky/pre-push`. `ls .github/workflows` returns nothing; the directory does not exist. `package.json` defines `"test": "vitest run --project unit"`, `"test:integration": "vitest run --project integration"` and `"test:all": "vitest run"`, but nothing in the repo invokes any of them automatically. So the only gate on every commit is type-and-lint, which is precisely the pair reported as "clean" in the 2026-08-04 and 2026-08-05 decision-log entries while 8 integration tests were red. Neither `pnpm typecheck` nor `pnpm lint` can observe a runtime fixture that has aged out — I ran both here and both are clean with the 8 tests still broken.
findings.impact: This is the mechanism that let a one-line fixture expiry survive 12 days, three decision-log entries, and a deliberate re-verification against a clean stash baseline without anyone diagnosing it. The integration project is where the tenant-isolation, RLS, billing-quota and reminder-correlation guarantees are actually asserted (the unit project cannot reach Postgres), and it runs only when a human remembers to and has Docker up. At launch, a regression in RLS or reminder quota would reach production the same way this fixture expiry did: silently, with a green pre-commit hook. Because the failures are now normalised in the log as an expected baseline, a genuine ninth failure appearing in that same file would very plausibly be absorbed into the same "the same 8 pre-existing failures" shorthand.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a GitHub Actions workflow on push/PR that runs `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, and — with a `supabase/postgres` service container plus `supabase start` or a bare Postgres matching `DATABASE_URL` — `pnpm test:integration`, so the integration project runs on every change rather than on recall. If a hosted runner for the Supabase stack is not wanted before launch, the cheaper interim is a `.husky/pre-push` that runs `pnpm test` (unit-only, ~21s, needs no Docker), plus deleting the "8 pre-existing failures" phrasing from the progress log once fixed so no future run treats a red integration suite as the baseline.

result.coverage_note: Ran `pnpm test` (unit project): 66 files / 637 tests, all passing, zero skipped, ~21s — no flakiness observed in the single run I did (I did not run it repeatedly, so I cannot speak to intermittent flake). Ran `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm lint`: both clean. Grepped the entire repo (excluding node_modules) with an extended regex for `it/test/describe.skip|.only|.todo|.skipIf|.runIf|.concurrent`, plus `xit`/`xdescribe` — ZERO hits anywhere, so no test is silently disabled; that part of the dimension is a genuinely empty report. Read the full `sendUpcomingReminderTemplate` describe block (app/(dashboard)/chat/__tests__/actions.integration.test.ts:308-690), the full implementation (app/(dashboard)/chat/actions.ts:197-464), `REMINDER_TEMPLATE_PRIORITY` in lib/inngest/functions/bootstrap-wa-connection.ts, `reminderQuotaAvailable` in lib/billing/usage.ts:508, tests/setup/global.ts, vitest.config.ts, and the 2026-08-01/04/05 entries in task-manager/progress.md. Verified the `handle_new_user` trigger exists (drizzle/migrations/0003, 0013) so the `innerJoin(pts)` in the action resolves — this is what rules out the alternative hypothesis that the failures come from a missing `pts` row (that would have failed the opt-out test too, giving 9 failures, not 8). WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK: I did not run `pnpm test:integration` — instructed not to, and it mutates the database. Note that the local Postgres IS reachable here (the vitest globalSetup connected and ran migrations during `pnpm test`), so the run was possible; I declined it on instruction. The 8-failure diagnosis is therefore static, but it is falsifiable and precise: the prediction is that all 8 fail with `{ ok: false, error: 'Nuk ka takim të ardhshëm.' }` and that `refuses the manual send to a patient who opted out of reminders` is the one that passes. I also could not verify that the other 63 integration files are still green as of today — the last recorded run was 2026-08-05 and three commits have landed since, so "63/64" is the log's claim, not something I confirmed. I checked the other integration files carrying near-past date literals (settings/services, lib/billing/reminder-usage, lib/today/queries, lib/appointments/availability, lib/billing/payments-extension) and all of them either inject an explicit `NOW` or do not compare the fixture against wall-clock, so none is a second time bomb.

Computed per WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance formula: #9ca2ae on white card (#ffffff) = 2.56:1; on the app background (#f3f3f0) = 2.31:1. AA requires 4.5:1 for normal text. `text-ink-3` is applied to real informational text, not decoration, in 79 call sites under app/(dashboard) and components/ (`grep -rn text-ink-3` count). Examples: connect-whatsapp.tsx:321 `

{note}

` (WhatsApp connection status note); profile-card.tsx:28 `` (practice subtitle); availability-editor.tsx:359 block-period date/time subtitle; client-detail.tsx:389 empty-state copy. This token was introduced by the Phase 14 'v2 New direction' re-skin (progress.md: shipped 2026-07-09) and extended in Phase 15 (2026-07-13); the only Lighthouse accessibility runs in the decisions log (96/100) predate both, on 2026-05-14 and 2026-06-19, so the regression has never been measured.
findings.impact: Every PT viewing secondary information — connection status notes, blocked-period subtitles, empty-state text, subtitle labels throughout settings and client screens — gets text that fails AA contrast by roughly half. findings.title: Chat message thread has no live region for inbound WhatsApp messages
findings.evidence: chat-thread.tsx:556 `<div className="flex-1 space-y-[11px] px-4 py-4">` is the container that maps over `visibleMessages` (from `useMessages`, lib/hooks/realtime.ts:293) and renders each `ChatBubble`. Neither this container nor any ancestor carries `aria-live`, `role="log"`, or `role="status"`. `useMessages` is backed by Supabase Realtime (confirmed via lib/hooks/realtime.ts:293-313, `mergeMessages`/`byId` state updated from a live subscription), so a new inbound patient message appended to the DOM while the screen reader user is elsewhere in the page — or while focus sits in the composer — produces no announcement at all; the only cue is `bottomRef.current?.scrollIntoView` (line 215), which is a purely visual affordance.
findings.impact: A screen-reader-using PT (or a sighted PT relying on TalkBack/VoiceOver for any reason) monitoring an open conversation gets no notification that the patient just replied unless they manually re-navigate the message list. Compare with sync-indicator.tsx, which does this correctly (`role="status" aria-live="polite"` at lines 13-14) — the chat thread is the one place in the app where 'something arrived' matters most and is the outlier that doesn't announce it.
findings.fix_sketch: Add `role="log" aria-live="polite" aria-relevant="additions"` to the messages container (or a visually-hidden `aria-live="polite"` region that announces "New message from {patientName}" on each realtime insert), matching the pattern already used in sync-indicator.tsx.

result.dimension: WhatsApp Embedded Signup v2/v3 → v4 migration (Meta hard cutoff 2026-10-15), including Graph API version pinning

findings.title: Signup client sends Meta's documented v2 `extras` shape plus the non-auto-upgradable `coex` feature type
findings.evidence: connect-whatsapp.tsx:180-189 calls `fb.login(..., { config_id: configId, response_type: 'code', override_default_response_type: true, extras: { setup: {}, featureType: 'whatsapp_business_app_onboarding', sessionInfoVersion: '3' } })`. Meta's Embedded Signup Versions page documents the extras object per version verbatim: v2 is `extras: { setup, features, featureType, sessionInfoVersion }`; v3 is `extras: { setup, features, featureType, version: "v3" }`; v4 is `extras: {} // The extras object is purposely empty for v4.` The repo's object contains `sessionInfoVersion` and no `version` key — an exact match for the v2 shape, and unambiguously not v4. The same page's table lists v2 (introduced Jan 2023) and v3 (May 29 2025) both as "Available Until: October, 2026", and the overview page carries the verbatim warning "Embedded signup v2 will be deprecated on October 15, 2026. Migrate your integration to v4 before that date to avoid disruption." Separately, `featureType: whatsapp_business_app_onboarding` is the Coexistence (`coex`) feature type, which Meta lists among the three feature types (`only_waba_sharing`, `marketing_messages_lite`, `coex`) that are NOT auto-converted to v4 and that "will no longer function; they will default to the standard embedded signup flow" after the cutoff. Docs used: https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/embedded-signup/versions , https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/embedded-signup/overview/ , https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/embedded-signup/implementation , https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/embedded-signup/version-4 .
findings.impact: On 2026-10-15 every PT who taps "Connect WhatsApp Business app" hits a retired flow. Best case the popup silently falls back to standard (non-coexistence) Embedded Signup, so a PT with an existing WhatsApp Business app number can no longer connect it and keep their history/contacts; worst case the flow errors before login and the product has zero onboarding path. Medium is pre-launch with coexistence as the *primary* onboarding path, so this removes the only way a real PT gets onto the product.
findings.fix_sketch: Create a v4 Facebook Login for Business configuration (Embedded Signup login variation, WhatsApp Cloud API product selected) and change the extras to `extras: { setup: {} }` — drop both `featureType` and `sessionInfoVersion`. These two changes must land together: with a v2 config and no `sessionInfoVersion` the `WA_EMBEDDED_SIGNUP` postMessage is never delivered, and the client's `if (!code || !wabaId)` branch at connect-whatsapp.tsx:199 would silently show the "incomplete" card. In v4 the Business-app path is not requested via extras — it is an outcome the user picks in Meta's UI, surfaced as the `FINISH_WHATSAPP_BUSINESS_APP_ONBOARDING` finish event. Verify against a live popup that the Business-app option actually appears before deleting the v2 config.

findings.title: `NEXT_PUBLIC_META_CONFIG_ID` still resolves to a v2 Login configuration and is build-time inlined
findings.evidence: whatsapp/page.tsx:38 reads `const configId = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_META_CONFIG_ID ?? ''` and passes it to `<ConnectWhatsApp configId={configId} …>` at lines 66 and 104; connect-whatsapp.tsx:181 forwards it as `config_id`. Meta's v4 implementation page states the version is now selected by the configuration, not by code: "A Facebook Login for Business configuration defines which permissions to request, and what additional information to collect, from business customers who access Embedded Signup", and the Versions page states "Selecting the products will automatically set you to v4." The repo's own phase note (task-manager/phases/02-whatsapp-integration.md:67) records that a wrong-but-well-formed config ID fails as a bare "Sorry, something went wrong" in the popup *before* login, with no diagnostic and no error code, and that "Config IDs are not readable through the Graph API (`GET /<configId>` returns `GraphMethodException` even with a valid app token), so this can only be checked by eye in the dashboard." The same file notes `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values are inlined at build time, so changing the config ID in Vercel needs a redeploy, not just an env-var save.
findings.impact: Even after the client extras are emptied to `{ setup: {} }`, the flow keeps running whatever version the existing configuration encodes. If that config is v2, onboarding still dies at the cutoff; if it is swapped without a redeploy, production keeps the old inlined ID and the change appears to have shipped while nothing changed. The failure mode is the undiagnosable pre-login popup error the team already lost a debugging session to on 2026-08-03.
findings.fix_sketch: Create a fresh v4 configuration in the Meta app dashboard (do not mutate the existing v2 one — keep it until the new one is proven), set `NEXT_PUBLIC_META_CONFIG_ID` to it in all three environments, and trigger a redeploy rather than only saving the env var. Re-check that the calling origin is in App Domains + Facebook Login for Business Allowed Domains for the new config, and re-verify the app-level `whatsapp_business_account` webhook fields (`messages`, `account_update`, `history`, `smb_app_state_sync`, `smb_message_echoes`) still apply under the v4 config.

findings.title: Connection mode is hardcoded `coexistence`; the FINISH event discriminator is captured then discarded
findings.evidence: connect-whatsapp.tsx:141-146 reads the postMessage as `if (typeof data.event === 'string' && data.event.startsWith('FINISH')) { sessionInfo.current = { phoneNumberId: data.data?.phone_number_id, wabaId: data.data?.waba_id } }` — `data.event` is used only as a boolean gate and the actual event name is thrown away. Line 215-220 then unconditionally POSTs `body: JSON.stringify({ code, phoneNumberId, wabaId, mode: 'coexistence' })`. The server reinforces the same assumption: route.ts:35 `mode: z.enum(['cloud_api','coexistence']).default('coexistence')`. Downstream, route.ts:90-92 runs `if (mode === 'cloud_api') { await registerPhoneNumber(phoneNumberId, token.accessToken) }` — i.e. `/register` is skipped for coexistence — and route.ts:348-351 writes `coexistenceSyncStatus: 'pending'` with a 24h deadline, which drives `syncWhatsappCoexistenceCore` (sync-whatsapp-coexistence.ts:44-63) to POST `${conn.phoneNumberId}/smb_app_data` with `sync_type` `smb_app_state_sync` and `history`. Meta's v4 implementation page documents `FINISH`, `FINISH_ONLY_WABA`, `FINISH_WHATSAPP_BUSINESS_APP_ONBOARDING`, `FINISH_OBO_MIGRATION`, `FINISH_GRANT_ONLY_API_ACCESS` as distinct outcomes of the *same* v4 flow, with `FINISH_WHATSAPP_BUSINESS_APP_ONBOARDING` meaning "user completed flow with a WhatsApp business app number".
findings.impact: Today the `coex` featureType forces every completion to be coexistence, so the hardcode happens to be right. After 2026-10-15 the feature type stops working and, per Meta, defaults to the standard flow — where a PT onboarding a brand-new Cloud API number produces a plain `FINISH`. That connection is still persisted as `mode='coexistence'`, so `/register` is never called and every outbound message the AI or the reminder job tries to send fails at the Graph layer (unregistered number), while `syncWhatsappCoexistence` fires `/smb_app_data` against a number that was never on the Business app, flipping the row to `coexistenceSyncStatus='failed'`. A PT appears connected in the PWA and silently sends nothing — patients get no replies and no reminders.
findings.fix_sketch: Store the finish event name alongside the ids in `sessionInfo.current`, and derive the mode from it: `FINISH_WHATSAPP_BUSINESS_APP_ONBOARDING` → `'coexistence'`, `FINISH`/`FINISH_ONLY_WABA` → `'cloud_api'`. Send that value in the POST body. Remove the `.default('coexistence')` from the zod schema so a missing `mode` is a 400 rather than a silently wrong branch, and add a route integration test asserting that a `cloud_api` payload calls `/register` and writes `coexistenceSyncStatus='not_applicable'` (route.integration.test.ts already exercises that branch at line 358, so the test harness exists).

findings.title: Tracker deadline note misstates which Embedded Signup version the app is on, understating the risk
findings.evidence: progress.md:60 reads "**2026-10-15 — Embedded Signup v2 retired.** Meta's migration target is v4; the client currently sends `sessionInfoVersion: '3'`", and phases/02-whatsapp-integration.md:60 repeats it verbatim and adds "Not yet owned by any phase — schedule it before the cutoff." Both conflate two unrelated contracts. `sessionInfoVersion` is the *session-info payload* version (Meta's Versions page documents it only under v2: partners "add a `sessionInfoVersion` to receive the callback", supported value `"3"`), while the *Embedded Signup* version is selected by `extras.version` — absent from connect-whatsapp.tsx:184-188 entirely. Meta's Versions table also retires v3 in October 2026 alongside v2, and the notes nowhere mention that `coex` (`featureType: whatsapp_business_app_onboarding`, connect-whatsapp.tsx:186) is on Meta's explicit no-auto-upgrade list.
findings.impact: The note reads as "we are on v3, v2 is what's being retired" and as a result the item is unowned by any phase with roughly eight weeks left. In reality the integration is on the retired version *and* on a feature type Meta will not migrate automatically, so the do-nothing outcome is total onboarding breakage rather than an automatic conversion. Anyone triaging the launch backlog from this note will deprioritise a blocker.
findings.fix_sketch: Rewrite both notes to state: extras shape matches Meta's documented v2 (no `extras.version`, `sessionInfoVersion: '3'`); v2 *and* v3 both retire October 2026; `coex`/`whatsapp_business_app_onboarding` is one of three feature types excluded from auto-conversion and requires manual migration; and the work is a new-v4-config + empty-extras + mode-discrimination change. Assign it to a phase with a date well before 2026-10-15 so there is room for a live popup re-test.

findings.title: postMessage origin check `endsWith('facebook.com')` accepts lookalike hosts
findings.evidence: connect-whatsapp.tsx:126-127: `function onMessage(event: MessageEvent) { if (!event.origin.endsWith('facebook.com')) return; …}`. `event.origin` is a full origin string, so `'https://evilfacebook.com'.endsWith('facebook.com')` is `true` — the guard admits any registrable domain whose name ends in the literal substring, not just Meta's origins. The accepted payload then populates `sessionInfo.current` (lines 142-145) with attacker-chosen `phone_number_id` / `waba_id`, which are POSTed to `/api/auth/meta-embedded` (line 215-220) and used verbatim by `resolvePhoneNumberId` and `persistConnection`. Meta's own sample code compares against the exact origin rather than a suffix.
findings.impact: A page the PT is browsing that holds a window handle to the Medium tab can inject a `WA_EMBEDDED_SIGNUP` FINISH message from a lookalike origin during an in-flight signup and substitute the WABA/phone ids. The exchanged `code` still comes from the real FB.login, so the practical outcome is a failed `subscribed_apps` call or a spurious `duplicate_number` 409 rather than a cross-tenant token — but it corrupts a security-relevant identifier on a path that has no other integrity check, and the fix is one line.
findings.fix_sketch: Parse the origin and compare exactly against Meta's origins — e.g. `const ok = event.origin === 'https://www.facebook.com' || event.origin === 'https://web.facebook.com' || event.origin === 'https://business.facebook.com'` — or at minimum check `new URL(event.origin).hostname === 'facebook.com' || hostname.endsWith('.facebook.com')`. Fold this into the v4 migration change since the listener is being touched anyway to capture the finish event name.

findings.title: The exact outage-causing redaction bug is still live: tokensOut/tokensIn/reasoningTokens/cachedTokens are redacted
findings.evidence: lib/log.ts:42 — `REDACT_KEY_RE = /phone|name|body|content|notes|email|token|secret|key|authorization|endpoint|p256dh|auth/i` matches any key CONTAINING the substring `token` (no word boundary). `tokensOut`, `tokensIn`, `reasoningTokens`, and `cachedTokens` all contain that substring and are NOT in `REDACT_ALLOWLIST` (lib/log.ts:50-57, which only has event_name/errorName/template_name/templateName/phone_number_id/phoneNumberId). I proved this against the real compiled module: `redactAttrs({tokensIn:120, tokensOut:0, reasoningTokens:4096, cachedTokens:10})` returns `{tokensIn:'[REDACTED]', tokensOut:'[REDACTED]', reasoningTokens:'[REDACTED]', cachedTokens:'[REDACTED]'}` (ran as a vitest case against lib/log.ts, then removed the scratch test). engine.ts:222-227 has a comment claiming these exact fields were added specifically because their absence caused the 2026-08-05 outage to be undiagnosable ('reasoningTokens and finishReason are here because their absence is what made a live empty-response outage un-diagnosable... a thinking budget that swallows maxOutputTokens shows up as exactly this pair'), but the fields are still silently redacted by `emit()` (lib/log.ts:167, `redactAttrs(rest)`), because they are not context keys (CONTEXT_KEYS = trace_id/pt_id/conversation_id only, lib/log.ts:130) and not allowlisted. `docs/observability/launch-log-review.md` §3 tells operators to read `ai.turn_completed`'s `tokensIn`/`tokensOut`/`cachedTokens` for spend/latency triage — those fields will read `[REDACTED]` in production today. No test in lib/__tests__/log.test.ts asserts these survive redaction (it only tests event_name/errorName/template_name/phone_number_id).
findings.impact: The next time an AI turn silently degrades (a thinking budget swallowing maxOutputTokens, a truncated response, a provider quietly changing token accounting) the operator is back to exactly the situation on 2026-08-05: reconstructing the request from scratch because the counts that would have diagnosed it in seconds all read [REDACTED]. This isn't a hypothetical — it is the literal previously-diagnosed failure mode, reintroduced by an allowlist that was never actually updated even though the code comment claims it was fixed.
findings.fix_sketch: Add tokensIn, tokensOut, reasoningTokens, cachedTokens (and any other count-only telemetry fields, e.g. costMicrousd already escapes since it doesn't match the regex) to REDACT_ALLOWLIST in lib/log.ts, or narrow REDACT_KEY_RE with word boundaries so 'token' doesn't match 'tokens*'. Add a regression test in lib/__tests__/log.test.ts asserting these specific keys survive redactAttrs — the existing allowlist test only covers name-shaped keys.

findings.title: No active alerting exists; the only 'monitoring' is manual, periodic human inspection of logs
findings.evidence: There is no Sentry (or any error-tracking SDK) anywhere in the codebase: no `@sentry` in package.json, no sentry* files, and `instrumentation.ts` only calls `assertEnvironmentIntegrity()` at boot — it does not wire any error reporter. This is a documented, deliberate 2026-05-06 decision (task-manager/progress.md:138: 'Sentry and PostHog are intentionally skipped for the current MVP because their free-tier limits are exhausted'), so I am not re-flagging the decision itself. What I am flagging is that nothing has filled the gap since, even after the decision's consequence played out live: `handleInboundMessage`'s onFailure (lib/inngest/functions/handle-inbound-message.ts:352-361) only writes a `conversation.failed` row to the in-app events/bell feed and sends the patient a fallback WhatsApp message — it never emits a proactive notification to the operator. `dispatch-push.ts`'s trigger list (lines 14-25) does not include `conversation.failed`, so even the PT is not pushed about a fully-exhausted AI turn; they'd have to open the PWA and see the bell. The `/admin` dashboard (app/(dashboard)/admin/page.tsx) has funnel/cost/billing widgets but no error-rate, failed-turn, or escalation-count metric at all, so even a proactive visit during an outage wouldn't surface it. docs/runbook.md's own 'Launch-week monitoring routine' confirms this is by design: 'Check Vercel logs, Supabase logs, and the operator dashboards several times a day for the first two weeks... then weekly.'
findings.impact: When production AI fails wholesale (as it did 2026-08-05, three exhausted Inngest attempts per message, repeatedly), nobody is paged. Discovery depends entirely on a PT or patient complaining, or the operator happening to check logs within their self-imposed 'several times a day' cadence — which is exactly the delay the referenced outage already experienced once.
findings.fix_sketch: Cheapest fix that doesn't reopen the Sentry cost question: have onFailure handlers (or a small Inngest cron polling `events` for a burst of `conversation.failed`/`ai.tool_failed` in a short window) push a webhook to something the operator actually watches (e.g. a Slack/Discord incoming webhook, or an email via the existing transactional-email provider) when failures exceed a threshold. Even a single 'more than N conversation.failed in 10 minutes' check on the daily-cost-rollup cron's cadence would have caught 2026-08-05 within the hour instead of on a complaint.

findings.title: Most background Inngest functions (reminders, billing, purge, resume) emit zero structured logs
findings.evidence: None of these nine files import `lib/log` at all (grep for `createLogger|logger\.` returns zero hits in each; confirmed the import lists directly for send-reminder.ts and appointment-events.ts — neither has an `@/lib/log` import). send-reminder.ts (741 lines) is the entire appointment-reminder pipeline — it calls `sendTemplate` (lib/channels/whatsapp/client.ts, which itself has no logging beyond one unrelated GDPR console.warn) and has no catch blocks at all (only two `throw new Error(...)`, lines 416 and 739); a failure just propagates to Inngest's own dashboard. appointment-events.ts (381 lines, appointment confirmation/cancellation sends) has the same shape. Contrast with the pipeline that IS well-instrumented: lib/conversation/engine.ts, the webhook route, lib/events/outbox.ts, lib/notifications/push-dispatch.ts, and poll-whatsapp-health.ts/reconcile-pok-orders.ts all call createLogger with trace_id/pt_id. Phase 11's own acceptance criterion (task-manager/phases/11-observability.md) is 'Filtering the chosen log sink by pt_id shows only that PT's logs' — for reminders, billing monitors, WhatsApp bootstrap, the AI-resume jobs, the purge cron, and template reconciliation, filtering by pt_id or trace_id returns nothing, because no log line carrying either was ever emitted.
findings.impact: A systemic bug in the reminder pipeline (a billed, patient-facing feature — e.g. a template getting silently rejected, a code regression in loadReminderAttempt, a WhatsApp API change) is invisible in the structured logs the runbook and launch-log-review checklist tell the operator to search. The only visibility is Inngest's own per-run dashboard (a different tool, not pt_id-searchable across runs) and the DB-level `reminder.failed` events/push notifications for individual failures — there is no way to spot a pattern ('every reminder today is failing') from the log sink the rest of the system is built around.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a `createLogger({trace_id, pt_id})` call at the top of each of these functions' step bodies (a `runId` fallback for trace_id, matching the pattern already used in handle-inbound-message.ts:368) and at minimum log the terminal outcome (sent/skipped/failed) of each reminder/appointment-event/billing-check with pt_id — mirroring the `ai.turn_completed`/`webhook.message_accepted` shape already used elsewhere.

findings.title: WhatsApp webhook's per-change dispatch loop has no top-level catch; a mid-batch throw loses trace_id correlation
findings.evidence: app/api/webhooks/whatsapp/route.ts POST (lines 55-112) generates a `trace_id` and iterates `parsed.data.entry[].changes[]`, calling `handleMessagesChange`/`handleStatusesChange`/`handleHistoryChange`/etc. directly with `await`, with no try/catch around the loop. Every log call inside those handlers is well-instrumented with `trace_id` (e.g. lines 121, 181, 411, 637, 810, 966, 1001 all do `createLogger({trace_id})`), but if any of them throws an uncaught exception (a DB error, a bug), the exception propagates straight out of `POST`, past every `log.*` call, and Next.js returns a bare 500 with no `event_name`/`trace_id`-tagged structured log line recording what failed — only whatever Next's default stderr stack-trace capture produces, which is not JSON, not filterable by trace_id, and not covered by docs/observability/launch-log-review.md's 'filter by trace_id' workflow (§5).
findings.impact: A change later in the batch failing (or a Meta payload shape this code doesn't defensively handle) surfaces only as an unstructured Vercel function-error stack trace, disconnected from the `trace_id` that ties the rest of that request's lifecycle together in the log-review workflow the runbook documents — the operator has to correlate by timestamp instead, which the runbook itself only proposes as a fallback for Supabase-side errors, not this case.
findings.fix_sketch: Wrap the `for (const entry...) for (const change...)` block in a try/catch that logs `webhook.change_processing_failed` with `{trace_id, field: change.field, ...serializeError(error)}` before returning (still 200, since Meta will otherwise redeliver the whole batch including already-processed, idempotent changes).

findings.title: Tenant-isolation/RLS write-open regression suite only runs under Docker, never automatically
findings.evidence: The 2026-07-30 audit found every tenant RLS policy was `FOR ALL TO authenticated` with default `GRANT ALL` to anon/authenticated — 'a PT could PATCH /rest/v1/pts and self-grant the paid Solo plan, delete their own audit_log, raise retention_days past the GDPR purge, or forge event_outbox rows that the publisher replays as trusted Inngest events' (progress.md, 2026-07-30 entry). The regression coverage for this — `tests/rls/coverage.integration.test.ts` ('every tenant policy is SELECT-only over the tenant predicate', 'anon and authenticated hold SELECT but no write privilege') and `tests/rls/isolation.integration.test.ts` (758 lines total, cross-tenant SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE matrix) — is entirely in the `integration` vitest project (`*.integration.test.ts`, filename pattern excluded from the `unit` project in vitest.config.ts). There is no `.github/workflows` directory in the repo (verified: `find .github -type f` returns nothing), `vercel.json`'s `buildCommand` is `pnpm check:migrations && pnpm build` (no test step), and `.husky/pre-commit` runs only `pnpm lint` && `pnpm typecheck`. `pnpm test` (the unit-only script) never touches these files.
findings.impact: The single worst defect class this project has actually shipped — cross-tenant write access that lets a PT alter or delete another tenant's billing/audit state, or forge trusted internal events — has a well-built, schema-driven regression suite, but nothing in the repo's automated path (build, pre-commit, or any CI) ever executes it. A future migration that reintroduces a permissive policy or a broad GRANT would pass lint, typecheck, and `pnpm build` cleanly and could reach `main`/production undetected unless a developer remembers to run `pnpm test:integration` with a local Docker Supabase stack up first. The decisions log shows the developer manually runs `test:all` at the close of each phase, which is a real mitigant, but there is no gate between those checkpoints.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a CI workflow (even a minimal one) that spins up the local Supabase/Postgres stack via Docker and runs `pnpm test:integration` on every push/PR to main and preview branches, or at minimum make `pnpm check:migrations` in the Vercel buildCommand also run the RLS coverage suite against the target DB before allowing a deploy to proceed.

findings.title: Duplicate-message regression test (2026-08-01 bug) only runs in Docker-gated integration tests
findings.evidence: progress.md's 2026-08-01 entry describes a real production bug: a patient who booked or rescheduled got two WhatsApp messages (the model's own confirmation plus the background job's deterministic one) because `appointmentEventPlan` returned `confirmPatient: true` unconditionally. The fix's own regression test is explicit about being 'the regression this whole change exists for' (comment at line 517-522 of `handle-inbound-message.integration.test.ts`): `it('sends exactly one WhatsApp message for an AI booking turn', ...)` drives both producers against one shared `sendFn` mock and asserts `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` plus exactly one `role='ai'` message row. This is the only place the two-producer interaction is exercised end-to-end, and the file is `*.integration.test.ts`, so it only runs via `pnpm test:integration` with Docker. The pure decision function `appointmentEventPlan` itself is unit-tested in `appointment-events.test.ts` (non-integration), but that only proves the plan object is correct in isolation — it does not exercise the actual two-producer race that caused the bug (the AI reply path and `handleAppointmentEvent` both attempting to send).
findings.impact: If a future change reintroduces a second unconditional sender (e.g. a new notification path added to the booking flow, or the `origin` field being dropped/defaulted incorrectly again), the only test that would catch a live double-send never runs in the normal edit-test-commit loop (no CI, and `pnpm test`/lint/build don't include it) — the exact same silent-regression risk that let the original bug ship.
findings.fix_sketch: Same fix as the RLS finding: get integration tests running in an automated gate. As a narrower mitigation, add a lightweight unit-level test that exercises `sendInboundReply` + `handleAppointmentEvent`'s plan-then-send logic together with mocked send functions (no real DB), so the two-producer contract has a unit-tier regression test independent of Docker availability.

findings.title: POK 404-vs-expired money-correctness fix has no unit test, only Docker-gated integration coverage
findings.evidence: The 2026-07-30 audit's own language: 'POK: a 404 returns a distinct not_found instead of pending, so an order is never terminally expired on an inconclusive poll (that state short-circuits every future settle — real lost money)'. `lib/billing/__tests__/pok-client.test.ts` (the unit test for the POK client) has zero occurrences of `not_found`, `404`, `expired`, or `pending` (grep returned nothing) — the distinction the audit fixed is not asserted at the unit level at all. The only coverage is `lib/inngest/functions/__tests__/reconcile-pok-orders.integration.test.ts`, e.g. `it('keeps re-polling an order POK answers with 404 while it is in budget', ...)` and `it('gives up on an order POK has not known for the whole budget', ...)`, both integration-only and Docker-gated.
findings.impact: This is a money-correctness path by the task's own definition (cap/entitlement money handling). A regression that collapses `not_found` back into `pending`/`expired` handling — the exact bug the audit fixed, which the audit explicitly called 'real lost money' — has no test that runs without a developer manually starting Docker and running `pnpm test:integration`. Given there is no CI, this is realistically the least-exercised safety net over an actual payments bug this project has had.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a unit test for the POK client's response classification (`not_found` vs `pending` vs `expired`) that mocks the HTTP layer only, independent of the Inngest reconciliation job and the DB — the classification itself doesn't need Postgres, only the surrounding scheduling logic does.

result.dimension: Reliability of the message pipeline and background jobs (Meta webhook → outbox → Inngest → AI turn → outbound WhatsApp send, reminders, booking transactions, external-call resilience)

findings.title: A non-text inbound (voice note, photo) leaves the patient in silence and is invisible to the PT
findings.evidence: `handleMessagesChange` (app/api/webhooks/whatsapp/route.ts:208-225): `if (msg.type !== 'text' || !msg.text) { log.warn('webhook.skipping_non_text_message', …); if (PATIENT_CONTENT_MESSAGE_TYPES.has(msg.type)) { … await bumpLastInboundAt(tx, conversationId, inboundAt); } continue; }`. The `continue` skips the `messages` insert, so there is no row, no `appendBackgroundEvent({type:'message.received'})`, no `tryPublishOutboxEvent`, and therefore no `handleInboundMessage` run — which is the only producer of the `conversation.needs_reply` push (handle-inbound-message.ts:431-443). The integration test at app/api/webhooks/whatsapp/__tests__/route.integration.test.ts:583-615 asserts exactly this: `expect(rows).toHaveLength(0); expect(sendSpy).not.toHaveBeenCalled();`. docs/observability/launch-log-review.md:64 files `webhook.skipping_non_text_message` under "expected noise … not launch-blocking".
findings.impact: An Albanian patient who sends a voice note (the dominant WhatsApp input mode in that market) or a photo of a referral/X-ray gets no AI reply, no acknowledgement, and no 'I can only read text' fallback. The PT is equally blind: because no `messages` row is written, nothing appears in the chat thread, no bell entry, no Web Push. The conversation's `last_inbound_at` is bumped so the PT *could* reply within the 24h window — but she is never told there is anything to reply to. The patient concludes the practice ignored them.
findings.fix_sketch: In the non-text branch, still persist a placeholder `messages` row (role 'patient', content e.g. a `[voice message]` marker, keyed on `external_id` for dedupe) and either (a) emit `message.received` and let the engine answer with a deterministic 'I cannot listen to voice notes, please write' reply, or (b) at minimum dispatch `conversation.needs_reply` so the PT is pushed and the thread shows the arrival. Option (b) alone is a small change and removes the silence-for-both-sides case.

findings.title: Meta webhook awaits an unbounded `inngest.send` (5 retries, no AbortSignal) inside the 20s ack budget
findings.evidence: app/api/webhooks/whatsapp/route.ts:271 awaits `tryPublishOutboxEvent(result.eventId)` per accepted message, inside the POST that must answer Meta. That calls `publishOutboxEvent` → `inngest.send(...)` (lib/events/outbox.ts:137-142). `lib/inngest/client.ts` constructs `new Inngest({ id: 'medium', schemas })` with no custom `fetch`, so the SDK uses the global fetch with **no timeout**, wrapped in `retryWithBackoff(fn, { maxAttempts: 5, baseDelay: 100 })` (node_modules/inngest/components/Inngest.js:499,580; node_modules/inngest/helpers/promises.js:157-168) — up to five sequential unbounded HTTP attempts per message. The webhook route also exports no `maxDuration`, whereas app/api/inngest/route.ts:13 sets one and its own comment says the implicit default may be "10s on a non-fluid Vercel function". lib/billing/pok/client.ts:121-131 proves the team knows the hazard: "Node's fetch has no default timeout worth the name (~300s per request)" and it wraps every call in `AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs)`.
findings.impact: When Inngest is slow rather than down (the common degradation — a fast connection refusal returns immediately, a hung socket does not), a batch of N inbound messages costs up to N × 5 unbounded requests before the webhook can answer. Meta drops the delivery at 20s and redelivers the whole batch, and Vercel may kill the invocation earlier at whatever the implicit default is. The DB insert has already committed, so nothing is lost — the once-a-minute outbox cron drains it — but every patient reply in that window is delayed by up to a minute while Meta hammers the endpoint with redeliveries of an already-processed batch.
findings.fix_sketch: Give the Inngest client a bounded fetch: `new Inngest({ id, schemas, fetch: (url, init) => fetch(url, { ...init, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(2000) }) })`, mirroring lib/billing/pok/client.ts. Optionally cap the immediate-publish path to one attempt (a dedicated send with maxAttempts 1) since the cron is already the durable retry, and add an explicit `maxDuration` to the webhook route so the platform ceiling is stated rather than inherited.

findings.title: `graphFetch` sends every WhatsApp Graph call with no timeout, so a hung socket burns the invocation
findings.evidence: lib/channels/whatsapp/graph.ts:44 — `const res = await fetch(url, { method, headers, body: … });` — no `signal`, no `AbortSignal.timeout`, and no per-call deadline anywhere above it (`authedGraph`/`sendFreeForm`/`sendTemplate` in lib/channels/whatsapp/client.ts just delegate). This is the single choke point for every outbound patient message (`sendInboundReply` → `sendFreeForm`, handle-inbound-message.ts:244-248) and every reminder template (`sendReminderTemplateOnce` → `sendTemplate`, send-reminder.ts:408-414), plus the quality/tier and coexistence polls. Contrast lib/billing/pok/client.ts:126, which does `fetch(url, { ...init, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs) })` for exactly this reason, and lib/conversation/engine.ts:189, which bounds the model call with `timeout: 30_000`.
findings.impact: A stalled TCP connection to graph.facebook.com holds the Inngest step until Vercel kills the invocation at the 60s ceiling (app/api/inngest/route.ts:13). The step is then retried; because `persistInboundReplyDelivery`/`persist-reminder-delivery` never ran, `messages.external_id` is still NULL, so the re-read guard in `sendInboundReply`/`sendReminderTemplateOnce` passes and the message is sent again — a duplicate WhatsApp message to the patient and, for reminders, a second Meta charge. It also blocks the per-conversation concurrency slot (limit 1) for the full 60s, stalling any follow-up message from the same patient.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a deadline in `graphFetch`: accept an optional `timeoutMs` (default ~10s for sends, shorter for polls) and pass `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs)`, translating `TimeoutError`/`AbortError` into a `GraphApiError` so the existing retry/`ConnectionRevokedError` classification still applies. That bounds the send at well under the 60s invocation ceiling and turns a hang into a fast, classified retry.

findings.title: POK reconcile's 4-minute in-step scan budget exceeds the 60s function ceiling it runs under
findings.evidence: lib/inngest/functions/reconcile-pok-orders.ts:53 sets `const SCAN_BUDGET_MS = 4 * 60 * 1000;` and the function deliberately runs the *entire* scan inside one step — the code comment says "The ENTIRE scan is one step" (reconcile-pok-orders.ts:230-236) — with up to `SCAN_LIMIT = 200` orders, each doing a network `applyOrderOutcome` poll. app/api/inngest/route.ts:13 caps that step at `export const maxDuration = 60;` with the comment "Every Inngest step body runs inside one request to this route, so the step's budget is this route's function duration." The step therefore can never reach its own 4-minute deadline; it is killed at 60s first, and the `pok.reconcile_budget_exhausted` warn at line 209 can never fire.
findings.impact: Once the open-order set is large enough that a scan exceeds 60s (200 orders × a POK round-trip is plausible during a POK slowdown, which is precisely when reconcile matters), the step is killed mid-scan instead of stopping cleanly, the run burns its 2 retries on the same overrun, and the hourly cron reports failure rather than partial progress. Settlement still converges because `applyOrderOutcome` is idempotent and per-order writes commit, but the intended graceful-degradation path is dead code and the operator sees a hard cron failure instead of the designed 'ran out of time, will continue next hour' signal.
findings.fix_sketch: Set `SCAN_BUDGET_MS` below the platform ceiling (e.g. 45_000) so the budget check actually fires and the run ends cleanly, or raise `maxDuration` on app/api/inngest/route.ts to 300 once fluid compute is confirmed and keep the two numbers explicitly paired with a comment. Cheapest correct fix today: derive the budget from a shared constant that is provably < maxDuration.

findings.title: A dead-lettered outbox row is stamped `published_at`, hiding it from any "never delivered" query
findings.evidence: lib/events/outbox.ts:164-190 — on the final failure `const exhausted = row.attempts >= MAX_PUBLISH_ATTEMPTS;` and the update applies `...(exhausted ? { publishedAt: new Date() } : { availableAt: … })`, i.e. an event that never reached Inngest gets the same `published_at` stamp as a successful publish (the only distinguishing mark is the `dead_letter: ` prefix in `last_error` and one `logger.error('outbox.publish_dead_lettered', …)` line). The same overloading happens for the trust-check path at lines 113-125 (`publishedAt: new Date()`, `lastError: 'rejected: …'`). docs/runbook.md:33-42 lists only `outbox.publish_failed` (the *transient* warn) as the thing to watch; the dead-letter error event name appears nowhere in the runbook, and no admin metric reads `event_outbox` (no non-test reference to the table outside lib/events/outbox.ts).
findings.impact: The poison-message handling is otherwise correct — `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` plus backoff means one bad row never blocks the queue, and nothing sits unpublished forever. But the drain is silent: a `message.received` row that exhausts 25 attempts (≈19h of retrying, e.g. across a rotated `INNGEST_EVENT_KEY`) means one patient's message is never processed at all, and the natural operational query — 'rows with published_at IS NULL' — returns zero. Detection depends entirely on someone reading logs for a single error line the runbook does not name.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a terminal `dead_lettered_at` (or a `status` column) instead of reusing `published_at`, so 'never delivered' is queryable; and add `outbox.publish_dead_lettered` to the docs/runbook.md Inngest section with the query to list such rows. A one-line count of dead-lettered rows in the existing /admin metrics would close it operationally.

findings.title: Patient phone numbers and wamids are written to platform logs, defeating lib/log.ts redaction and GDPR erasure
findings.evidence: lib/log.ts:41-42 defines `REDACT_KEY_RE = /phone|name|body|content|notes|email|token|secret|key|authorization|endpoint|p256dh|auth/i` and the file header promises "NEVER log tokens, phone numbers, patient names, or message bodies". Three attr keys in use match none of those alternatives, so they pass through verbatim: (1) app/api/webhooks/whatsapp/route.ts:682 `wa_id: waId` inside `log.warn('webhook.contact_sync_failed', ...)`, where line 664 sets `const waId = contact.wa_id ?? phone;` and line 651 sets `const phone = contact?.phone_number;` — i.e. the value is literally the patient's phone number; (2) app/api/webhooks/whatsapp/route.ts:211 `externalId: msg.id` in `log.warn('webhook.skipping_non_text_message', ...)` — msg.id is a Meta wamid; (3) lib/inngest/functions/handle-inbound-message.ts:411, :505, :539 `wa_message_id: delivery.messageId` in `log.info('inbound.reply_sent'|'inbound.capped', ...)`. The only value-level defence is `valueScrub` (lib/log.ts:64-66) which replaces `/\+\d{7,15}/g`; a WhatsApp wa_id is E.164 digits with NO leading `+` (e.g. `355691234567`), so it is not matched. The repo already classifies a wamid as personal data: drizzle/migrations/0026_reminder_deliveries.sql states "A wamid embeds the recipient's phone number, so it is NOT anonymous and cannot simply be left behind", and lib/patients/erase.ts:123-130 acts on that by rewriting `reminder_deliveries.external_id` to `'erased:' || id` during erasure. lib/__tests__/log.test.ts covers `phone`, `phone_number_id` and nested objects but has no case for `wa_id`, `externalId` or `wa_message_id`, so nothing catches these.
findings.impact: Every inbound non-text message, every AI reply, and every failed contact sync writes a patient's phone number (or a wamid that encodes it) into Vercel and Supabase log storage in cleartext. Those logs sit outside the database, so a GDPR Article 17 erasure run through lib/patients/erase.ts — which deliberately scrubs the same identifier from reminder_deliveries — leaves the identifier intact in the log store, and the retention purge in lib/inngest/functions/purge-expired-messages.ts cannot reach it either. For a medical-adjacent product in the EU this is a data-minimisation and erasure-completeness defect that a DPA review at launch would flag, and it widens the blast radius of any log-access compromise from 'uuids and counts' to 'the PT's actual patient list'.
findings.fix_sketch: Add `wa_id`, `waId`, `externalId`, `external_id`, `wa_message_id`, `wamid` and `recipient` to REDACT_KEY_RE in lib/log.ts (or, better, invert the design to an explicit allowlist of loggable keys since the current regex is already carrying six ad-hoc alternatives), extend `valueScrub` to also strip bare 8-15 digit runs and `wamid.` prefixed tokens, and add cases to lib/__tests__/log.test.ts asserting each of the three call sites redacts. The call sites themselves should log `pt_id` + the internal `message_id` uuid, which are already present and sufficient for correlation.

findings.title: POK settlement credits a full plan period on isCaptured alone without checking the captured amount or currency
findings.evidence: lib/billing/payments.ts:105-109 is the whole authenticity decision for a payment: `function classifyPokStatus(order: PokOrder) { if (order.isCaptured) return 'paid'; if (order.isCanceled || order.isRefunded) return 'failed'; return 'pending'; }`. `settleOrder` (lib/billing/payments.ts:275-310) then extends the plan unconditionally — it reads `row.period` from the ledger, computes `computeExtendedExpiry(previousExpiresAt, row.period, now)` and writes `plan: 'solo', planExpiresAt: newExpiresAt` — without ever comparing `order.amount` to `row.amountMinor` or `order.currencyCode` to `row.currency`. Both fields are available on the fetched order: `orderSnapshot` at lib/billing/payments.ts:112-123 persists `amount: order.amount ?? null` and `currencyCode: order.currencyCode ?? null` into `billing_orders.pok_payload`, so the values are read and stored but never asserted against what was ordered. The re-fetch design (`applyOrderOutcome` line 176 onward) is otherwise correct — the ledger row's `ptId`, `period` and `amountMinor` all come from the authenticated `createCheckout` path, never from the webhook body.
findings.impact: If POK's hosted payment page ever permits a captured amount that differs from the amount on the created order (partial capture, a client-side editable amount, or a currency mismatch), the settle path credits a full month or year of Solo regardless of what was actually taken, and the discrepancy is silently recorded in pok_payload rather than rejected. This is money-correctness on the only revenue path in the product. I could not prove POK allows this — the repo itself documents that POK's contract is undocumented and the staging spike could not authenticate (see the header comment in app/api/webhooks/pok/route.ts) — so this is reported as an unvalidated authoritative field, not a demonstrated exploit.
findings.fix_sketch: In settleOrder, before flipping status to 'paid', compare the re-fetched order against the ledger row: if `order.amount` is present and !== `row.amountMinor`, or `order.currencyCode` is present and !== `row.currency`, do not extend the plan — log a distinct `pok.amount_mismatch` event and leave the row in 'created' for manual review. Keep the existing FOR UPDATE mutex and idempotency unchanged; this is one guard clause inside the already-locked transaction.

findings.title: Conversation cap silently disables safety escalation for the patient
findings.evidence: handle-inbound-message.ts:467 `if (gate.status === 'at_cap') {` sends the static cap handoff and returns at :507 `return { capped: true, handoffSent: true };` — before the AI turn at :519 `turn = await step.run('run-ai-turn', () => runInboundTurn(context));`. The ONLY deterministic safety check lives inside that turn: engine.ts:676 `const safetyReason = detectSafetyEscalation(context.inbound.content, context.escalationKeyword);` followed by :683 `await escalateForSafety(context, safetyReason);` which flips `aiActive=false` via `escalate_to_human`, emits `conversation.escalated`, pushes the PT, and replies with `safetyEscalationResponse(...)`. Nothing upstream of the cap gate calls `detectSafetyEscalation` — grep over handle-inbound-message.ts returns no hit. The only reply the patient gets is cap-handoff.ts:23 `CAP_HANDOFF_MESSAGE_SQ = 'Faleminderit për mesazhin! Do t’ju përgjigjemi personalisht sa më shpejt.'`. The paused path was deliberately built to preserve escalation (engine.ts:683-691 escalates first, then throws `assistant_paused`), and the C2 decisions-log entry says so explicitly — the at-cap path was not given the same treatment, so this reads as an omission, not an accepted trade-off. No test in lib/billing/__tests__ or lib/inngest/functions/__tests__ covers safety at cap.
findings.impact: A patient of a PT who has hit the monthly conversation cap writes 'dhimbje në gjoks', 'urgjencë', 'nuk mund të marr frymë', or the PT's own escalation keyword. They receive a bland 'we will answer you personally soon', the conversation is NOT flipped to human, no `conversation.escalated` event is emitted, and the PT gets no push — the thread looks like any other AI-handled thread in the inbox. On the Free plan (30 conversation-days/month) this state is reachable in a normal month, and it converts a billing limit into a clinical-safety regression for the exact message class the product treats as never plan-gated.
findings.fix_sketch: Run `detectSafetyEscalation(context.inbound.content, context.escalationKeyword)` in handle-inbound-message.ts before the `at_cap` branch (or hoist the whole safety block into a step that runs regardless of the gate result). On a hit, take the normal escalation path — dispatch `escalate_to_human`, emit `conversation.escalated`/push, send `safetyEscalationResponse` — instead of the static cap handoff. The conversation-day fact is already compensated-deleted at cap, so an escalated turn stays unmetered and the cap is not weakened. Add a regression test asserting an at-cap inbound containing an urgent-health phrase escalates and pushes.

findings.title: BILLING_PLAN_OVERRIDES can re-arm the reasoning/maxOutputTokens outage with no load-time guard
findings.evidence: plans.ts:141 `reasoningEffort: z.enum(['low', 'medium', 'high'])` is a first-class field of the override schema, deep-merged per environment at plans.ts:231-234 and resolved at module load from `process.env.BILLING_PLAN_OVERRIDES` (plans.ts:236). models.ts:84 passes it straight through (`reasoningEffort: base.reasoningEffort`) and client.ts:31-32 puts it on the wire (`if (config.reasoningEffort) settings.reasoning = { effort: config.reasoningEffort };`). The counterpart is still a bare literal: engine.ts:187 `maxOutputTokens: 500`. Per the doc comment at plans.ts:22-36 and the 2026-08-05 decisions-log entry, OpenRouter derives the thinking budget as `max(min(max_tokens*ratio,128000),1024)`, so at 500 EVERY effort level lands on the 1024 floor and exceeds the whole allowance. Nothing asserts the pairing: models.ts has `assertProductionPrivacy()` at :44 for the privacy invariant, but there is no equivalent for this one, and the env registry describes the var only as 'JSON override of plan limits, for testing caps' (env-vars.ts:249-253). A single Vercel production env value — `BILLING_PLAN_OVERRIDES={"free":{"model":{"production":{"reasoningEffort":"low"}}}}` — reproduces the exact shipped outage, and 'low' looks like the safe choice to whoever types it.
findings.impact: The override exists precisely for emergency tuning without a deploy, i.e. it is used under pressure by someone not reading plans.ts's doc comment. Setting any effort value makes every model turn on which the model actually thinks return no text; `runModelTurn` throws `empty_response`, which is retryable, so all three Inngest attempts fail identically, the patient gets the technical-failure handoff and the thread is escalated. It is intermittent (a simple booking turn emits 0 reasoning tokens), so it degrades production for hours before anyone correlates it, and it fails at request time rather than at boot.
findings.fix_sketch: Move the 500 out of engine.ts into a leaf constant (e.g. `lib/ai/limits.ts` exporting `MODEL_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`) imported by both engine.ts and lib/ai/models.ts. In models.ts, beside `assertProductionPrivacy()`, add `assertReasoningBudgetFits()` that iterates `PLAN_IDS × APP_ENVS` over the resolved `PLANS` and throws when a config sets `reasoningEffort` while `MODEL_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS <= max(min(MODEL_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS*ratio,128000),1024)`, naming the plan/env and the required max_tokens. Call it at module load so a bad override fails the boot and the test run, not a patient conversation.

findings.title: Settle credits a full plan period without checking the amount or currency POK actually captured
findings.evidence: `classifyPokStatus` (payments.ts:107-111) returns 'paid' on `order.isCaptured` alone. `settleOrder` (payments.ts:273-335) then writes `status:'paid'`, `pokPayload: orderSnapshot(order)` and `pts.plan='solo'` with the extended expiry, never comparing `order.amount` / `order.currencyCode` to the ledger row's `amountMinor` / `currency` that `createCheckout` stored at payments.ts:169-177. The data is right there — `orderSnapshot` (payments.ts:114-124) deliberately persists `amount: order.amount ?? null, currencyCode: order.currencyCode ?? null` — it is just never asserted against. The whole minor-unit question hangs on one constant with no runtime check: payments.ts:91 `const ALL_MINOR_FACTOR = 1;`, confirmed only by reading a STAGING hosted page (scripts/smoke-pok.ts:166-181), and read-model.ts:195-198 then reports `amountAll: row.amountMinor` — our number, not POK's — on the PT's receipt.
findings.impact: If POK production interprets the integer amount differently from staging (the factor-1 evidence is a staging screenshot, and `orderSchema.amount` is `z.coerce.number()` because POK stringifies numbers), a PT is charged 25 ALL instead of 2 500 and still receives a full month of Solo, while the receipt at /settings/billing, `billing_orders.amount_minor` and the admin monthly CSV all report 2 500. Every downstream record agrees with itself and disagrees with the bank, so the discrepancy is invisible until reconciliation with POK's own statements. The same blind spot covers any partial capture or currency mismatch.
findings.fix_sketch: In `settleOrder`, before extending the plan, compare the authoritative order against the ledger row: if `order.amount` is present and `!== row.amountMinor`, or `order.currencyCode` is present and `!== row.currency`, do not credit — log an `error`-level `pok.amount_mismatch` with both values and the order id and return a distinct result so the reconcile cron surfaces it instead of silently retrying. Keep crediting when POK omits the fields (tolerant schema), so the check hardens the normal path without turning a missing field into a lost payment.

findings.title: Live checkout renders unconditionally while POK credentials are not required in production
findings.evidence: `LIVE_PAYMENTS_ENABLED` no longer exists anywhere in the tree (grep over *.ts/*.tsx returns nothing); commit 0c80fae wired the live checkout. page.tsx:108-127 renders `<CheckoutForm …/>` whenever `snapshot.price && slot.kind` is upgrade/switch/renew, and `snapshot.price` is always non-null because it comes from `getPlan('solo').price` (read-model.ts:174, plans.ts:123). The credentials that path needs are declared optional everywhere: env-vars.ts:221-240 marks `POK_MERCHANT_ID`, `POK_KEY_ID` and `POK_KEY_SECRET` `requiredIn: NONE`, with a now-false description — 'Live checkout stays gated until set'. Nothing gates on them; `requirePokEnv` (payments.ts:49-54) throws `POK_MERCHANT_ID is required` on the first real checkout, which `createCheckoutAction` surfaces to the PT as the generic `toast.error(t.billing.checkoutFailed)` in checkout-form.tsx:37-39.
findings.impact: If the production deployment goes live before the POK secrets land in Vercel — which is exactly the pre-launch sequence the tracker describes — `pnpm check:env` passes, the billing screen shows a working 'Paguaj' button and every PT who tries to upgrade gets 'Pagesa dështoi' with no explanation and no server-side alarm (the reconcile cron's outage throw only fires once at least two open orders exist, and none can be created). The result is a launch where the single revenue path is dead and looks like a payment failure to the customer.
findings.fix_sketch: Move `POK_MERCHANT_ID`/`POK_KEY_ID`/`POK_KEY_SECRET` to `requiredIn: DEPLOYED` (or at least `['production']`) so `check:env` blocks a deploy without them, and fix the stale description. Separately, have `getBillingSnapshot`/`resolveCheckoutSlot` receive a `paymentsConfigured` flag derived from the presence of the POK env vars, and render the existing `t.billing.paymentsComingSoon*` copy instead of the pay button when it is false — restoring an explicit gate rather than an exception behind a generic toast.

findings.title: Downgrade deactivates services and re-upgrade never restores them, with no notice either way
findings.evidence: `runDowngrade` (billing-renewal-monitor.ts:177-191) flips every active service except the oldest to `active:false` via `UPDATE services SET active=false … WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM services WHERE pt_id=… AND active=true ORDER BY created_at ASC LIMIT ${maxActive})`. The re-upgrade path does the opposite of restoring it: `settleOrder` (payments.ts:308-311) sets only `{ plan: 'solo', planExpiresAt: newExpiresAt, planDowngradedAt: null }` — no services touched. Neither notification mentions services: push-payload.ts:171-178 for `billing.downgraded` says 'Plani Solo skadoi. Rinovo kur të duash për ta rikthyer.', and the bell copy at format.ts:162-167 is 'Kalove te plani Falas'. The retention side of the same downgrade IS auto-lifted on re-upgrade (`planDowngradedAt: null` feeds `effectiveRetentionDays`), which shows the asymmetry is unintended rather than a stated policy.
findings.impact: A PT with four services lapses, gets downgraded to one active service, then pays to renew. They are back on Solo with `maxActiveServices: null`, but their assistant still offers exactly one service to every patient — bookings for the other three quietly stop — and nothing in the app told them their services were switched off or that they must switch them back on. They have paid 2 500/25 000 ALL for a plan that under-delivers until they happen to open /settings/services.
findings.fix_sketch: Either reactivate on settle — inside `settleOrder`'s transaction, re-enable services deactivated by the downgrade (record the downgrade timestamp on the service row, or scope by `pt_id` when the new plan's `maxActiveServices` is null) — or, at minimum, make the loss explicit: include the deactivated-service count in the `billing.downgraded` event payload and say so in the push/bell copy, and add a dismissible banner on /settings/services after a downgrade. The reactivate-on-settle option is the one that matches 'downgrade deletes nothing'.

findings.title: Meta EUR-zero placeholders are known categories, so re-categorised traffic prices as free
findings.evidence: meta.ts:57-64 ships `marketing: 0` and `authentication: 0` as `⚠ CONFIRM` placeholders alongside the confirmed `utility: 21_000`. The safety net that exists — meta.ts:72 `META_RATE_CARD_UNKNOWN_CATEGORY_MICRO_EUR = 21_000`, documented as 'so an unknown BILLABLE message is never silently free' — does not apply here, because `metaRateForCategory` (meta.ts:141-148) checks `isKnownCategory(normalized)` first and 'marketing' IS known, so it returns 0. `metaCostFromBillableCounts` only reports `unknownCategories` (meta.ts:174), so daily-cost-rollup.ts:155-159 logs nothing for a zero-rate known category. Medium submits templates as `category: 'UTILITY'` (lib/channels/whatsapp/client.ts:299, :324), but the pricing category on the delivered message comes from Meta's own `pricing.category` field, which Meta can and does re-assign.
findings.impact: Confined to reporting: every consumer of the rate card is `cost_daily` (daily-cost-rollup.ts:150-175) and the ADMIN_EMAILS-gated dashboards (metrics/admin.ts:276-291, :734-786) plus the GDPR export. No cap, entitlement, gate, or charge reads Meta cost, so this cannot change product behaviour. But if Meta re-categorises a reminder template to MARKETING, the billable messages are priced at zero with `meta_cost_source='actual'` and no warning line — and the Free-plan COGS card, the one number that says whether the free tier is survivable at launch, reads zero for that traffic.
findings.fix_sketch: Make the placeholder status structural rather than a comment: keep a `PLACEHOLDER_CATEGORIES` set for the two unconfirmed rates and have `metaRateForCategory` return `META_RATE_CARD_UNKNOWN_CATEGORY_MICRO_EUR` for them until `META_RATE_CARD_OVERRIDES` supplies a real value, and have `metaCostFromBillableCounts` report them in the same warn channel as `unknownCategories` so the rollup logs when placeholder-priced traffic appears. Replace with the real Meta rates during the pre-launch pricing re-check.

findings.title: Downgrade mutex hardcodes the grace window instead of using EXPIRY_GRACE_DAYS
findings.evidence: The pure decision core derives the boundary from the config constant — billing-renewal-monitor.ts:76 `const graceEndMs = expMs + EXPIRY_GRACE_DAYS * DAY_MS;` (imported from plans.ts:131) — but the authoritative write that actually performs the downgrade re-checks it with a literal: billing-renewal-monitor.ts:169 `sql` fragment `${pts.planExpiresAt} + interval '3 days' <= ${now.toISOString()}::timestamptz`. The two agree only because `EXPIRY_GRACE_DAYS = 3` today; the same constant also drives `resolveEffectivePlan`'s live entitlement window (entitlements.ts:40) and the 'grace' state and `daysLeft` on /settings/billing (read-model.ts:117-124), so it is a value someone would plausibly tune in one place.
findings.impact: Shortening EXPIRY_GRACE_DAYS makes `planRenewalActions` return `downgrade` while the in-transaction WHERE still refuses, so `runDowngrade` returns false on every run and no lapsed PT is ever downgraded — the cron reports `downgrades: 0` and looks healthy. Lengthening it does the reverse: entitlements still honour Solo while the write has already flipped the row to Free. Either way the divergence is silent, and the money-path write is the half that disagrees with the config.
findings.fix_sketch: Bind the constant into the statement instead of writing it twice — e.g. `${pts.planExpiresAt} + (${EXPIRY_GRACE_DAYS} * interval '1 day') <= ${now.toISOString()}::timestamptz` — so the decision core and the mutex cannot disagree, and add a test that changes the constant and asserts both halves move together.

findings.title: The plans help page still tells PTs that paying is not possible yet
findings.evidence: help/plans/page.tsx:85-89 reads 'Hapi i pagesës po shtohet ende. Për momentin do të shohësh njoftimin “Pagesat vijnë së shpejti”; sapo të aktivizohet, do të mund ta përfundosh pagesën direkt aty' — it quotes a banner that no longer exists. The strings it quotes, `paymentsComingSoonTitle` / `paymentsComingSoonBody` (lib/i18n/dict/billing.ts:65-67), have no consumer left anywhere in app/, components/ or lib/ (the only surviving `comingSoon` uses are the Dual/Multi plan chip in landing-page.tsx:395 and an unrelated channel chip). Meanwhile /settings/billing renders a live `CheckoutForm` with a working 'Paguaj' button (page.tsx:108-127).
findings.impact: This is the only Albanian-language page explaining how to upgrade, and it is linked from the help index. A PT who reads it concludes that upgrading is not yet possible and does not attempt it — on a launch whose entire monetisation is one self-serve checkout. A PT who tries anyway finds the app contradicting its own help page on the first money screen they see, which is the worst place for the product to look unfinished.
findings.fix_sketch: Rewrite the 'Si të kalosh te Solo' section to describe the shipped flow: pick monthly or yearly, get redirected to POK's hosted page, return to /settings/billing where the order settles and Solo activates. Delete the now-dead `paymentsComingSoonTitle`/`paymentsComingSoonBody` keys, or keep them and wire them to the missing-POK-credentials gate proposed in the checkout-gating finding so the copy is true again in that one case.

findings.title: Any inbound WhatsApp sender becomes an AI-processed patient with no consent gate
findings.evidence: `ensureWhatsappConversation` (app/api/webhooks/whatsapp/route.ts:741-782) runs on every inbound WhatsApp message and unconditionally does `tx.insert(patients).values({ptId, name, phone: waId, waId}).onConflictDoNothing(...)`, then creates a `conversations` row. It is called from `handleMessagesChange` for every `value.messages` entry (line 229) with zero check of whether the sender has ever interacted with the practice or consented to anything. `conversations.aiActive` defaults to `true` (schema.ts line 244), so the AI assistant engages and forwards message content to OpenRouter/Anthropic/OpenAI on the very first inbound message. Separately, `handleAppStateSyncChange` (line 626) ingests the PT's entire WhatsApp Business App address book into `whatsapp_contacts` (name, phone, wa_id) via coexistence `smb_app_state_sync`, with no filter distinguishing patients from any other contact in the PT's phone. The project's own progress log (task-manager/progress.md, 2026-07-30 entries) records this exact gap as finding **F39** — "every Business-app contact the PT messages becomes a patient record and a future AI target" — and explicitly lists it as **deferred**, not accepted/won't-fix, alongside other items that *were* closed that same session.
findings.impact: A person who has no relationship with the practice (a supplier, a family member, a wrong number, or any contact synced from the PT's real WhatsApp Business App) can have their message content sent to a third-party AI processor and stored as "patient" data the moment they text the connected number or the moment their contact card syncs in — with no notice, no consent capture, and no way for Medium (or the person) to tell them apart from an actual patient before the fact. This undermines the controller/processor consent structure the ToS relies on (the PT is contractually told to obtain patient permission, but the system does not require or verify that before AI processing begins), and exposes bystander data to the AI subprocessors named in the privacy policy.
findings.fix_sketch: Gate `ensureWhatsappConversation`/AI engagement behind an explicit PT confirmation step for first-time senders (e.g. conversation starts in a 'needs review' state, AI stays paused until the PT marks the sender as a patient), and stop auto-materializing `whatsapp_contacts` rows into candidate AI targets — keep contact sync for name-lookup only, not as an implicit consent signal.

findings.title: Synced address-book contacts have no retention limit or erasure path unless matched to a patient
findings.evidence: `whatsapp_contacts` (schema.ts:172-192) stores `phone`, `waId`, `fullName`, `firstName` for every contact the coexistence sync ingests (route.ts:626-686), with only a soft `deletedAt` set when Meta reports a removal — the row itself is never purged. The nightly retention job (`purgeExpiredMessages` / `purgePtExpiredMessages`, lib/inngest/functions/purge-expired-messages.ts) only deletes from `messages`, `events`, and `audit_log`; it never touches `whatsapp_contacts`. The only deletion path for that table is inside `erasePatient` (lib/patients/erase.ts:104-106), which deletes rows matching a specific patient being erased via `patientWhatsappContactsFilter`. A contact who is never turned into (or matched to) a `patients` row — e.g. anyone in the PT's phone who is not a patient — has no age-based purge and no DSAR/erasure mechanism at all.
findings.impact: Third-party personal data (names and phone numbers of the PT's non-patient WhatsApp contacts) is retained indefinitely with no storage-limitation control and no way for that person to ever get it erased, contrary to GDPR Art. 5(1)(e) storage limitation and Art. 17 erasure — since they are not a "patient" in Medium's data model, none of the product's DSAR/erasure UI can reach them.
findings.fix_sketch: Either exclude non-patient-matched contacts from long-term storage (purge whatsapp_contacts rows with no matching patient after N days), or fold them into the same retention window as messages/events, and give the PT a way to request/trigger deletion of a specific synced contact independent of patient erasure.

findings.title: Privacy policy names only Anthropic/OpenAI though production also routes through AWS Bedrock
findings.evidence: `docs/gdpr/subprocessors.md` and `app/(legal)/privacy/ai-providers.ts` (`DISCLOSED_AI_PROVIDERS = { anthropic: 'Anthropic', openai: 'OpenAI' }`) — rendered verbatim into the live Albanian privacy policy via `disclosedAiProviderNames()` — name only Anthropic and OpenAI as the upstream AI processors. The project's own progress log (task-manager/progress.md, 2026-08-04 entry) states: "**All Anthropic models route via Amazon Bedrock under ZDR, not Anthropic-direct** — `docs/gdpr/subprocessors.md` still names Anthropic as the upstream and does not reflect this; flagged deliberately rather than rewritten, since whether AWS becomes a named sub-processor is a legal characterisation." This was written after the privacy policy's last `updatedAt` stamp (30 korrik 2026) and remains unresolved in the current code — no AWS/Amazon Bedrock entry exists anywhere in the subprocessor list or the disclosed-providers guard.
findings.impact: The production model actually processing patient conversation content runs on AWS infrastructure that is not disclosed anywhere the PT or patient can see, so the subprocessor list the DPA and privacy policy point to is inaccurate for the live production routing — a GDPR Art. 28(2)/13(1)(e) disclosure gap that the team has already identified but left open.
findings.fix_sketch: Add Amazon Web Services (Bedrock) as a named subprocessor in docs/gdpr/subprocessors.md and the privacy policy (or confirm via OpenRouter/Anthropic's DPA that Bedrock routing is legally covered by the Anthropic subprocessor entry and document that reasoning explicitly), then update the `ai-providers.ts` guard/test to reflect whatever the resolution is.
